title: Early hemodynamic assessment and longitudinal imaging for predicting graft outcomes post-transplant

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Early hemodynamic assessment and longitudinal imaging for predicting graft outcomes post-transplant》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p4】Given the poor prognosis of EAD, we aimed to assess if early postoperative ultrasound flow parameters could detect it early. However, these parameters were only effective in the first postoperative week, limiting their long-term prognostic use. Therefore, we explored whether additional imaging features from longitudinal grayscale ultrasound could predict long-term graft-related adverse event-free survival (GRAEFS) outcomes, aiming for a comprehensive solution from early detection to long-term follow-up. (Figure 1).

【Introduction · S0001-p1】Liver transplantation (LT) is vital for treating end-stage liver disease [1], but complications like early allograft dysfunction (EAD) can impact patient prognosis and graft survival [2]. EAD occurs in 20–40% of cadaveric liver transplants [3]. Current EAD prediction models like Early Allograft Function (MEAF) [4] and Liver Graft Assessment Following Transplantation (L-GrAFT) [5], despite being validated, struggle with issues like complexity [6], lack of external validation [7], and diverse cohorts [5], hindering their clinical adoption.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Early hemodynamic assessment and longitudinal imaging for predicting graft outcomes post-transplant》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Research design and participants · S0002-S2001-p1】This study is a multicenter retrospective investigation conducted in compliance with the Declaration of Helsinki and received approval from the Institutional Review Board of Xiamen University Affiliated Xiang’an Hospital (Xiamen Center), Guizhou Provincial People’s Hospital (Guiyang Center), and the Second Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University (Dalian Center). Given the retrospective and non-invasive nature of the study, informed consent was waived. The study report was meticulously prepared following the TRIPOD + AI guidelines [16]. Based on predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, a total of 341 patients who underwent orthotopic LT from deceased donors were included in the study, comprising recipients of grafts from both brain-dead and cardiac-dead donors (E1.1). To investigate the application of artificial intelligence in the imaging prognosis of LT, patients from the Xiamen and Guiyang Centers were randomly allocated into a training set and an internal validation set in a 7:3 ratio, while patients from the Dalian Center served as an external validation set (Figure S1).

【Research design and participants · S0002-S2001-p2】Inclusion criteria for the study were as follows:patients undergoing orthotopic cadaveric LT;availability of comprehensive clinical data;availability of complete and uninterrupted ultrasound examination data and image records within 1-year post-surgery.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Early hemodynamic assessment and longitudinal imaging for predicting graft outcomes post-transplant》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Model performance based on longitudinal ultrasound images · S0003-S2002-S3002-p1】According to landmark analysis principles, Delta features and model evaluations were limited to patients without a graft-related adverse event by each time point (Table S7). This study utilized a transfer learning framework based on the Vit b/16 architecture. The model underwent training for 50 epochs, with continuous monitoring of the F1 score and AUC on the validation set to identify the optimal model. Consequently, the model from epoch 26 was selected as the deep learning feature extractor, achieving the highest F1 score (0.868) and AUC (0.822) on the validation set, thereby demonstrating superior classification performance and discriminative capability. Subsequently, this model was employed to extract deep learning features from all images. Detailed information on Delta feature selection (Table S8) and the risk scoring formula (E1.10) is available in the (supplementary materials Figure 4). Based on the Delta feature risk scores at six distinct time points, we developed radiomics nomogram (Figure 3A) and Vit b/16 nomogram (Figure 3B).

【Model performance based on longitudinal ultrasound images · S0003-S2002-S3002-p2】The model’s performance evaluation results in the training cohort, as well as the internal and external validation cohorts, are presented in Figure 4. The Vit b/16 nomogram exhibited superior discrimination, calibration, and overall predictive accuracy across all cohorts when compared to the radiomics nomogram. In the external validation cohort, the Vit b/16 nomogram achieved a 3-year AUC of 0.831 (95% CI: 0.730–0.933), surpassing that of the radiomics nomogram, which recorded an AUC of 0.779 (95% CI: 0.661–0.898). DeLong tests confirmed that this difference was statistically significant in both the internal validation cohort (p = 0.047) and the external validation cohort (p = 0.032). In terms of calibration, the Vit b/16 nomogram produced a calibration intercept of 0.347 and a calibration slope of 0.628 in the external validation cohort; its Brier score was 0.213, which is lower than the 0.238 observed for the radiomics nomogram, indicating reduced predictive error. A sensitivity analysis, conducted after excluding tumor recurrence events, revealed that the AUCs for both models across all cohorts varied by less than 0.05 compared to the primary analysis. This finding suggests that the model performance is not significantly affected by the inclusion of the tumor recurrence component within the GRAEFS composite endpoint, thereby affirming the robustness of the study’s conclusions (Table 2).

【Data availability statement · S0007-p1】The datasets used and analyzed during the current study are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

【Ultrasound image preprocessing and radiomics analysis · S0002-S2004-p2】Utilizing the PyRadiomics software package (version 3.0), a total of 1409 radiomics features were extracted from the ultrasound images at each time point following LT for each patient. To quantify the longitudinal dynamic changes, we calculated the Delta radiomics characteristic, which is defined as the net relative change between the characteristic values on postoperative days 7, 30, 60, 90, 180, and 365, compared to the baseline value on postoperative day 1. To prevent time-related bias, this study uses a landmark analysis framework (E1.4).

Utilizing the PyRadiomics software package (version 3.0), a total of 1409 radiomics features were extracted from the ultrasound images at each time point following LT for each patient. To quantify the longitudinal dynamic changes, we calculated the Delta radiomics characteristic, which is defined as the net relative change between the characteristic values on postoperative days 7, 30, 60, 90, 180, and 365, compared to the baseline value on postoperative day 1. To prevent time-related bias, this study uses a landmark analysis framework (E1.4).
